name: Jim Walton
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2026); SEC insider holdings (2024)
forbes_bio: Jim Walton is the youngest son of Walmart founder Sam Walton (d. 1992).
He is chairman of the family's Arvest Bank Group, which boasts assets of $28 billion.
Jim sat on Walmart's board for more than a decade before yielding the seat to his son, Steuart, in 2016.
Collectively, he and other heirs of Sam Walton own about 45% of Walmart's stock.
Jim's daughter Annie Proeitti chairs the family's $8.6 billion (2024 assets) Walton Family Foundation.
forbes_facts: Jim majored in business administration at the University of Arkansas.

name: David Sun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); Wikidata (2016)
forbes_bio: David Sun cofounded and helps run Kingston Technology, which makes storage and memory products, as COO from a cubicle on the sales floor.
With longtime partner John Tu, Sun launched a computer memory business out of a garage and sold it to now defunct PC maker AST a few years later.
The pair started Kingston by making surface-mount memory chips after losing most of their first fortune in the stock market.
Sun and his wife, Diana, have a foundation that provides grants to education programs for under-served youth in the U.S. and Taiwan.
The company's name comes from one of John Tu's favorite bands, the Kingston Trio.
forbes_facts: Sun met longtime business partner John Tu in a basketball league in 1978.

name: Wang Liping
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2007-2026)
forbes_bio: Wang Liping is the chairman of Shanghai-listed Jiangsu Hengli Hydraulic, which makes oil cylinders, hydraulic valves and hydraulic castings.
Wang founded the company in 1990. Today it has seven research centers and 12 manufacturing sites in China, Germany, the U.S., Japan and Mexico.
Hengli's clients include Caterpillar, Kobelco and China's Sany Heavy Industry.
Hengli opened a 141,000-square-meter factory in Mexico in 2025 to serve customers across the Americas.

name: Ravi Jaipuria
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022)
forbes_bio: India's cola king, Ravi Jaipuria, presides over RJ Corp. which is into everything from beverages and fast food to healthcare and education.
His listed flagship Varun Beverages is one of PepsiCo's biggest bottlers outside the U.S.
The youngest of three brothers, Jaipuria studied in the U.S. and returned home in 1985 to join the family business as a bottler for Coca-Cola.
After a family division in 1987, in which he got one bottling plant as his share, he switched to PepsiCo.

His Devyani International, which operates KFC, Pizza Hut and Costa Coffee stores, which got listed in 2021, agreed to merge with rival Sapphire Foods in a $934 million deal in January 2026, creating a fast food giant.
forbes_facts: Varun Beverages is named after his son and Devyani International after his daughter.
Jaipuria also has a stake in hospital chain Global Health (Medanta), which went public in 2022.
His son Varun got married in a small ceremony at the family's Delhi home in 2020 amid pandemic lockdown restrictions.
The Gurgaon-based Pepsi bottler has entered new segments like dairy; sports drinks and fruit juices that are powering its growth.

name: Steven Rales
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Steven Rales and his brother Mitchell acquired a REIT in 1983 and merged it into their firm Danaher, named after a Montana creek.
Focused on tax avoidance and cash flow, they acquired more than three dozen companies and turned Danaher into a diversified firm.
Rales serves as chairman of the board at Danaher, which had around $24 billion in sales in 2024.
In 2021, he and his brother each transferred Danaher shares worth more than $1.5 billion to their charitable foundations.
In 2023, Rales purchased an additional 15% stake in the NBA's Indiana Pacers; he now owns 20% of the franchise.
forbes_facts: His production company Indian Paintbrush funded some of Wes Anderson's movies, such as "Isle of Dogs", "Moonrise Kingdom" and "The Grand Budapest Hotel."
His brother Mitchell Rales showcases his extensive art collection in a state of the art museum in Maryland.

name: Hasmukh Chudgar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Low profile Hasmukh Chudgar founded generics maker Intas Pharmaceuticals in 1977.
Chudgar has long handed over operations to his sons Nimish and Binish, who run the $3.5 billion (revenue) company.
In August 2025, Intas Pharma acquired biosimilar company Udenyca from California-based Coherus Life Sciences for $558 million.
The company's portfolio includes an affordable drug to treat breast cancer called Eleftha, which is similar to Roche's Herceptin.
In 2022, the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority bought a 3% stake in Intas from Temasek.
forbes_facts: Chudgar's third son Urmish heads the company's biopharma business and is a haematologist-oncologist.
The company's biggest markets are Europe and India.

name: Ali Ghodsi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Ali Ghodsi is cofounder and CEO of software startup Databricks, which private investors valued at $134 billion in February.
After a career in academia, Ghodsi cofounded Databricks with six UC Berkeley academics who built the popular analytics engine Apache Spark.
Databricks is built on top of Spark and uses AI to power, in Ghodsi's words, a "data lakehouse" that helps companies store and utilize their data.
Ghodsi was tapped to lead Databricks in 2016 amid company struggles to generate revenue; initially, he had joined in 2013 as a part-time engineer.
The first-time CEO orchestrated a turnaround after revamping Databricks' leadership and product offerings.
forbes_facts: Ghodsi is a Swedish citizen, who arrived in the country as a child after his family was forced to flee Iran during the 1979 Revolution.

name: Marcos Galperin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Marcos Galperin is founder of e-commerce platform MercadoLibre, the eBay of Latin America.
MercadoLibre, which operates in 18 Latin American countries and Portugal, went public in 2007 on the Nasdaq.
In 2026, after 26 years at the helm, Galperin stepped down as CEO and became executive chairman of the company.
He worked at Argentine oil company YPF for three years and as a summer intern at JPMorgan before starting MercadoLibre in 1999.
forbes_facts: eBay, once MercadoLibre's largest shareholder with 18%, sold its stake in 2016 for more than $1 billion.
Galperin helped organize Argentina's first-ever presidential debate ahead of the country's 2015 elections.
Galperin hails from Argentine business royalty. His grandfather started Sadesa, a tannery that has grown into one of the country's largest leather manufacturers.

name: Cai Haoyu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun China (2022-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2023-2026); Hurun China U40 (2022); Hurun Unicorn founders (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Cai Haoyu is a cofounder of Shanghai-based online games developer miHoYo, which he established in 2012 with college friends, Liu Wei and Luo Yuhao.
He stepped down as miHoYo chairman in 2023 for unexplained reasons and handed the reins over to Liu, but continued to retain a large stake.
Best known for its Genshin Impact adventure game, the company develops products that often feature anime-style characters and rich storylines.
Also in 2023, Cai cofounded Anuttacon, which focuses on developing AI-powered games. It released in 2025 Whispers from the Star, an interactive game featuring an AI companion named Stella.
Liu and Luo are both billionaires.
forbes_facts: Apple CEO Tim Cook described miHoYo as a "phenomenal team" after a visit to its Shanghai headquarters in 2023.

name: Jiang Rensheng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2010-2026)
forbes_bio: Jiang Rensheng is the chairman of Shenzhen-listed vaccine firm Chongqing Zhifei Biological Products.
A longtime distribution partner of Merck, Zhifei won the Chinese sales rights to the U.S. pharma's HPV drug in 2018.
In 2023, Jiang took his antibody drug maker Chongqing Genrix Biopharmaceutical public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.
Prior to striking out on his own, he worked as a primary school teacher and a government health official.
In 2024, Zhifei entered an exclusive partnership with GSK, a pharma headquartered in the UK, to distribute shingles vaccines and explore RSV vaccine commercialization in China.

name: Rodger Riney
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Rodger Riney is the cofounder of discount brokerage firm Scottrade, which is now part of Charles Schwab.
After college, Riney turned down a job at a top engineering firm and joined a Missouri investment company for less pay.
A decade later, he quit his job, drove 1,500 miles from St. Louis to Scottsdale, Ariz. and cofounded Scottrade in 1980.
Riney, who bought out his partner in 1985, expanded the firm to 3 million client accounts with a total of $170 billion in assets under management.
He sold out to Joe Ricketts' TD Ameritrade for $4 billion in 2017, 2 years after he was diagnosed with blood cancer multiple myeloma.
He has since donated $40 million to Washington University in St. Louis  to research the disease and develop treatments for neurodegenerative illnesses.
